finding.claim: /fetch2 fetches an attacker-supplied URL with only a scheme check. Internal hosts, loopback and cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) are reachable, and redirects are followed by default.
finding.sink: requests.get(url, timeout=5) at views.py:22; the response body (first 200 chars) is returned to the caller

trace.note: url taken from the query string
is_http_url only checks that the scheme is http or https
requests.get with redirects enabled; body reflected in the JSON response

finding.guards_checked: is_http_url checks the scheme only. There is no host or IP filtering, no allowlist, and no redirect restriction, so the guard does not prevent SSRF.

verdict.guard_found: none (is_http_url at validators.py:7 is a scheme-only check; the stronger is_safe_url is only used on /fetch, not /fetch2)
verdict.reason: views.py:19-22 passes the query-string url through only the scheme check at validators.py:7 into requests.get(url, timeout=5) with default redirects and reflects the body, so internal and metadata hosts are reachable.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the URL by resolving the hostname in is_safe_url, then requests.get resolves it again. A DNS-rebinding attacker can return a public IP for the check and an internal IP for the fetch. This is a TOCTOU weakness and is lower confidence than finding 1.
finding.sink: requests.get(url, timeout=5, allow_redirects=False) at views.py:14; the response body is returned to the caller

trace.note: url taken from the query string
socket.getaddrinfo resolves the hostname once for the check
rejects private, loopback, link-local and reserved addresses
requests.get resolves the hostname a second time, so the result can differ

finding.guards_checked: The scheme check, the resolved-IP blocklist and allow_redirects=False are all present and block direct internal URLs and redirect-based bypasses. The remaining gap is that the validated IP is not pinned to the connection. The blocklist also does not use ip.is_global, so some special ranges such as multicast are not rejected.

verdict.guard_found: Scheme check plus a resolved-IP blocklist (validators.py:12-17) and allow_redirects=False (views.py:14). None of these is hostname set membership or an anchored match, and the validated IP is not pinned to the connection.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches: views.py:11 reads the query-string url, validators.py:14 resolves it for the check, and views.py:14 calls requests.get, which resolves it again with no IP pinning. This leaves a DNS-rebinding TOCTOU window that the blocklist at validators.py:16 does not close.
